_readme: THE HAND-EDITED HALF of the work gallery. tools/bake_work.py reads this plus
the masters beside it and writes work.json, which script.js renders.
Every piece in a category's folder is SHOWN unless its stem is in `omit`, so
dropping a file in is all it takes to publish it, and pruning is one line.
bake_work.py prints how many it showed and how many it omitted per category
on every run — a category that quietly stopped finding art is a failure, not
a clean pass.
frames  the card's rotating carousel, in order. Frame 0 is the card's
thumbnail AND item 0 of the category, so clicking the card lands
on the piece it was showing. Add or remove freely; five is not a
rule. Frame 0 is the only one that also appears in index.html.
pos     stem -> object-position, overriding the one tools/focal_point.py
measures. Nothing is cropped on disk, ever. You should rarely need
this: the measured value keeps heads in frame automatically, and
the one entry here is knights-of-edengale-3, an interior where the
top of the picture is ceiling rather than a subject.
zoom    stem -> how far to tighten the CARD's cover-crop: a number, or
{ scale, pos } to tighten around a point of its own rather than
around the measured one. object-position can
only PAN a crop, and a piece with a painted border, or a
turnaround sheet where the character is a fifth of the width,
needs it tightened instead. Not the filmstrip thumb -- a thumb
has to look like the piece it opens -- and not the hero, which
fits the whole picture. Use sparingly: this throws away pixels.
order   projects, best first. A PROJECT is a stem minus its trailing -N,
so all five brigadier-bluebeard files move together -- the gallery
never splits one. Anything not named here follows alphabetically,
so a new folder appears on its own, just at the back.
titles  project stem -> display title, where the stem does not title-case
cleanly. A project is the stem minus its trailing -N, so all five
brigadier-bluebeard files share one title.
notes   project stem -> the caption's second line. Defaults to the
category label. THESE ARE THE PLACEHOLDER: tools and years are
not recorded anywhere yet, so nothing here claims them.
STATUS 2026-09-01: first pass. The categories, the frame picks and the omit
lists are a starting point to look at and cut down, not a settled taxonomy.
